 ORDER

This is the first criminal appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14- A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 20 of 2023 registered at Police Station Dheerpura, District Datia (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 457, 354, 294, 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(d)(dh) and added 376 of IPC and Section 3(1)(w-ii) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

sentences.text:
Prosecution story in brief is that the prosecutrix filed a written complaint on 04.03.2023 that at 1:00 A.M. in night, when she was sleeping in the house with her children and her husband had gone to field, at that time, the appellant entered in the house and grabbed her right hand but as then she Nandram Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99426584/
1 shouted the appellant fled away.

sentences.text: Thus, on the said written complaint by the prosecutrix, a case was registered against the appellant, but later on during recording of her statements uner Section 164 of CrPC, she levelled allegations of commissioner of rape, accordingly, offence under Section 376 of IPC and 3(1)(w)(ii) of the SC and ST Act were enhanced.
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that on a demand being made by the applicant of returning his money, the report had been made.
The appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.
Further argument is that the appellant is in custody since 19.04.2023, the prosecutrix is major.
Investigation is nearing completion, therefore, there is no requirement of further custodial interrogation of the appellant.
The appellant has no criminal antecedents.
Learned counsel further submits that appellant is permanent resident of District Datia (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Hence, learned counsel prays for grant of bail to the appellant.
O n the other hand, learned State counsel as well as counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the appeal and prayed for its dismissal.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the conduct of the prosecturix, without commenting upon the merits of the case, this appeal stands allowed and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rs.
One Lakh only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court.

The appellant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and 6. The appellant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
A copy of this order be sent to the Court concerned for compliance.
